Q: Private Cloud Run service returns generic HTML 404 with no request log A:

Well, looking at what you described, the key detail here is that generic HTML 404 page and the total lack of request logs.

Basically, your request is not even reaching your app container at all. It is getting stopped and rejected at Google's front door (the Google Front End / GFE load balancer) before it ever gets routed into Cloud Run.

Here is what is likely going on, mapped to your questions:

1. Why you get a generic HTML 404 with zero logs

When Google's frontend returns that classic 404 HTML page without writing anything to Cloud Run request logs, it almost always means one of these things:

  • Host header mismatch: If your HTTP client altered or stripped the original Host: header, Google’s front edge doesn't know which service you are trying to reach and just drops a generic 404.
  • Typo or missing region in the URL: If the hostname does not match an active route registered on Google's edge tables (for example, hitting an old, mistyped, or non existent hash subdomain), the frontend simply says "not found" at the infrastructure level.
  • DNS caching or propagation lag: If the service was created and tested immediately, edge routing tables occasionally take a few seconds to sync up worldwide.

Since the request never gets handed over to the Cloud Run service infrastructure, no request log or trace entry is created.

2. Are status.url and the deployment output URL both callable?

Yes, absolutely. They both point to the exact same default endpoint (https://<service>-<hash>-<region>.a.run.app). For a private service, you just need to pass a valid Authorization: Bearer <ID_TOKEN> header where the token's audience matches that base URL.

3. How to tell a frontend routing miss apart from an IAM rejection

You can easily tell them apart by the HTTP status code and response body:

  • Frontend Route Miss (404 Not Found): Returns the standard Google 404 HTML page. Zero Cloud Run logs because Google's edge doesn't recognize where to send the traffic.
  • IAM Rejection (403 Forbidden): Cloud Run's builtin auth layer will intercept the call and return a 403 Forbidden with a plain text or specific error message (e.g., Your client does not have permission to get URL...), not a generic 404.

So, um, double check your custom HTTP client to make sure it sends the full, untouched Host header matching the exact .a.run.app address, and verify there wasn't a tiny typo in the URL path or domain name.
